# fix(redteam): shard 1f round-1 — UNIQUE idx + raw_execute guard + hermetic unit suite

**Commit**: `578fd9f7fdbe` — fix(redteam): shard 1f round-1 — UNIQUE idx + raw_execute guard + hermetic unit suite

**Body**:

Round-1 redteam (reviewer + security-reviewer, both CLEAN on load-bearing
axes) surfaced 5 LOW findings + 1 same-class test-isolation gap; all fixed
in-shard per autonomous-execution MUST-4.

- Account blind-index indexes are now UNIQUE (security LOW-4). The inbound
  resolver's LIMIT 1 assumes one account per blind index; UNIQUE makes that
  structural (closes a signup race + hardens any future Account-creation path).
  NULLs stay distinct under PG UNIQUE so pre-backfill rows don't conflict.
  Regression test: test_duplicate_blind_index_rejected_at_db_layer.
- SessionCrud.raw_execute now enforces its read-only contract — rejects any
  statement not starting with SELECT/WITH (security LOW-1 / quality L3), so a
  future caller can't route DDL/DML through it.
- Inbound email "no_account" log masks the destination inbox (to=_mask_email),
  matching the WhatsApp sibling (security LOW-3); 1f made this the hot path.
- WhatsApp resolver docstring softened: = ANY(:phones) makes no ordering
  guarantee (quality L1).
- Unit suite is now hermetic against a shell that exports ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY
  (same-class gap surfaced during verification). A tests/unit/conftest.py
  autouse fixture forces the no-key regime for ALL unit tests; the inbound
  resolver (1f) and the learning loop (1b) both bifurcate on the master key and
  their unit fakes only implement the no-key path. Tests that need a key mock
  `sequor.config.settings` itself (provisioning) or stub the boundary (erasure)
  and are unaffected.

Deferred (out of 1f scope): email dev-branch casing asymmetry (quality L2 —
pre-existing, unreachable via signup in pure-dev); constant-time burn on the
absent-account branch (security LOW-2 — inbound is a signed-webhook inbox-
resolution path, not a credential path; wrong tradeoff).

Receipts:
- unit (clean env):          438 passed, 1 xfailed
- unit (master key exported): 438 passed, 1 xfailed  (was 12 failed pre-guard)
- tier2 full:                51 passed, 1 xfailed
- 1f tier2:                  5 passed (incl. UNIQUE regression)
